name: Brotli decoder RCE
tile_line: In Node.js, .NET, Envoy, Python. In CISA KEV.
tldr: A bug in the Brotli decompressor can crash apps, leak memory or run code when they unpack outside data. Attacks have started; it's on CISA's exploited list. It's in Node.js, .NET, Envoy and many Python apps: update them and rebuild images.
summary: Unpacking outside Brotli data is common: HTTP clients such as Python's requests decompress Brotli responses on their own, and Express 5 request bodies can carry it. broccoli2shell.com first described code execution only on a deliberately weakened build, but ELLIO reproduced the public exploit on official, unmodified Node.js builds with default settings, and its sensors saw it in attacks.

affected.label: A vulnerable Brotli copy
affected.text: Brotli 1.0.3–1.2.0 (except the patched 1.0.10 and 1.1.1), Node.js below 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1 (including 20, 23 and 25, which get no fix), .NET 8/9/10, Envoy/Istio, or Python `Brotli` / `brotlicffi` below the fix, and PHP for Windows before the 26 Oct rebuilds. On RHEL, Node 22, Node 24 on RHEL 10 and .NET 9/10/11 use the system libbrotli, so update that package too; Node 24 on RHEL 8/9 and .NET 8 bundle their own copy. .NET Framework, Java's own decoder and pure-JS/Rust ports use other code and aren't affected; Java JNI wrappers, PHP and Ruby extensions and Go cgo bindings around the C library are. `process.versions.brotli` only shows Node's bundled copy, so check `node -v`.
affected.cmd:
node -v
pip show Brotli brotlicffi
dpkg -l | grep -i brotli

affected.label: You decompress outside Brotli data
affected.text: Node's `fetch()` or `zlib` Brotli APIs, Express 5 request bodies, Python requests/urllib3/aiohttp with a Brotli package installed, .NET `HttpClient` auto-decompression, ASP.NET Core request decompression or BrotliStream/BrotliDecoder (off by default), PHP's cURL with auto-decompression, or Envoy/Istio with the Brotli decompressor turned on. A bare `node:http` server doesn't decompress.

do.label: Update the runtime
do.text: Install the latest safe version for your line (listed below); it also fixes later bugs. Node.js 20, 23 and 25 get no fix, and .NET 8 and 9 reached end of life on 10 Nov 2026. Also: PHP for Windows 8.5.12-1 / 8.4.27-1 / 8.3.36-1 / 8.2.35-1, and Brotli itself 1.0.10 / 1.1.1 / 1.2.1.

do.label: Rebuild container images
do.text: Patching the host doesn't fix copies baked into images. Rebuild, redeploy, and bump lockfile pins.

do.label: Stopgap: block br request bodies
do.text: Reject `Content-Encoding: br` request bodies at your proxy or WAF. This doesn't cover responses your app fetches.

changes.text: Corrected: ELLIO reproduced the public exploit on official, unmodified Node.js builds and saw it in attacks, so it isn't limited to a weakened build. Java JNI wrappers around the C decoder are affected too. Added the GitHub advisory for the Python Brotli packages.
Added Istio 1.32 to Safe versions (Istio lists 1.32.0 and later as patched).
RHEL bundling corrected (Node 24 on RHEL 8/9 and .NET 8 carry their own copy). .NET 11.0.0 is out; .NET 8 and 9 reached end of life. Safe versions added.
Review: full Envoy and Node version lists, RHEL system-library note, PHP for Windows, exploit caveat.
Microsoft: container images must be rebuilt.
Added to CISA KEV. Verdict raised to Patch now.
